solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Official politician touring city where people scoff

indicators.note: going round, so the two outer pieces travel around the city's letters

parts.note: a referee is a sports official, REF for short
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
EC is the postcode area for the City of London

explanation.surface: A referee who is also a Conservative politician makes a tour of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' is informal British for eating greedily, not mocking; the definition describes a dining hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A refectory is a communal dining hall in a monastery or college, a place where people eat.

clue.text: Was a criminal half-heartedly clad like a judge?

indicators.note: losing half of the heart, so one of the two central doubled letters goes

parts.note: a criminal who stole was said to have robbed

explanation.surface: A puzzled question: was this criminal only half-hearted, dressed up as a judge?
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' removes one B of the central pair BB in ROBBED.
explanation.definitionFit: Judges sit in court wearing long gowns, so a judge is dressed in robes.

clue.text: Fellow serves state: it preserves honour

parts.note: aces are unreturnable serves in tennis
to aver is to state or declare

explanation.surface: A man serves his country, and that keeps his honour intact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serves' looks like a verb about duty, but it is tennis: aces are winning serves.
explanation.definitionFit: A face-saving gesture or excuse lets someone keep their dignity and avoid humiliation.

clue.text: Playing cousin Tom first in rugby union or league

indicators.note: playing about with the letters rearranges them into a new order
the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A cousin called Tom gets his first game, playing in either rugby union or rugby league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' shuffles COUSINTOM with R, the first letter of 'rugby'. 'Union or league' looks like the two codes of rugby but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A consortium is an association or alliance of companies or groups, like a union or league.

clue.text: Elevated thus, stood for chancellor once

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means reading it from the bottom up

parts.note: so means thus, in that way
past tense of putting up with something: stood, tolerated, endured

explanation.surface: Raised up this way, a politician stood for the office of chancellor in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated' turns SO upwards to give OS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: George Osborne was the UK Chancellor of the Exchequer from 2010 to 2016, so a former finance minister.

clue.text: Less mature guy, one off on run

indicators.note: something off is wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A rather immature man takes a day off, going for a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like time off work, but signals a rearrangement of the first two words' letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of fewer years means being less grown up, so the comparative of youthful fits.

clue.text: Endless, boring work plugged by current singers

indicators.note: a hole plugged by something has that thing pushed into it
without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a chore is a dull routine task
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: An endless, tedious task gets interrupted by a surge of electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts CHORE to CHOR; 'plugged by' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is an organised group of people singing together, as in a church.

clue.text: Dice the buccaneer keeps rolling over

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters read in the opposite direction
the words hold the letters within them, keeping them inside

explanation.surface: A pirate keeps rolling the dice over and over at the gambling table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' finds EBUC inside 'the buccaneer'; 'rolling over' turns it round. Buccaneer is also this setter's pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To dice food is to chop it into small even blocks, each a little solid square.

clue.text: TV personality's revolutionary version of Marx

indicators.note: something that revolves turns round, so the name reads backwards

parts.note: Harpo was one of the Marx Brothers comedy team

explanation.surface: A television star is a revolutionary take on Karl Marx.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' and 'Marx' suggest Karl, but the Marx here is the comedy brothers; HARPO reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Oprah Winfrey is the famous American talk-show host and broadcaster.

clue.text: Swimmer's possibly East German hairdo

parts.note: a communist is a red, and East Germany was a communist state
a mullet is a haircut short at the front and long at the back

explanation.surface: An East German swimmer is identified by a distinctive hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Swimmer' means 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The red mullet is a fish of the Mediterranean and Atlantic, so a swimming creature.

clue.text: Painter's possible reason to have to walk back

indicators.note: read back, so the letters go in reverse order

parts.words: possible reason to have to walk
parts.note: having no cab, no taxi, is one reason someone must go on foot

explanation.surface: The artist may have had a reason for walking home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NO CAB round. The 's after 'Painter' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was a celebrated Irish-born British artist of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Oaf collared by teacher cried

indicators.note: held round the neck, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teaching degree
a lubber is a clumsy, stupid fellow

explanation.surface: A clumsy lout, grabbed by a schoolteacher, burst into tears.
explanation.walkthrough: BEd, Bachelor of Education, is the British teaching degree; the oaf goes between its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To blubber is to weep noisily, so the past tense means wept.

clue.text: Record how old we are to cause despair!

parts.note: a vinyl record is a disc
our age is the number of years we have lived

explanation.surface: Putting our age on record would only make us gloomy!
explanation.definitionFit: To dishearten someone, sapping their confidence and hope, is to make them lose heart.

clue.text: Grand, as you once may have been

definitions.meaning: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars

definitions.text: as you once may have been
definitions.meaning: the old familiar form of address to one person, used in Shakespeare and the Bible

explanation.definitionFit: Short for thousand, it means a grand; it was also the archaic singular form of 'you'.

clue.text: Run after Jesus's birth with man of God

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, dates years after the birth of Christ
a minister is a clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes charge of the services after Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: To run an organisation is to manage or govern it, to be in charge of its affairs.

clue.text: Choose to enter river in buff

indicators.note: going in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
to vote is to choose by ballot

explanation.surface: Someone decides to go into the river naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in buff' suggests 'in the buff', naked, but 'buff' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A buff is an enthusiast, a keen fan of a subject such as film or history.

clue.text: Friar's party vessel holding a little beer?

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
a mini can is a small tin of beer

explanation.surface: A monk's celebration features a container holding a small amount of ale.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Friar' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dominican is a member of the Order of Preachers founded by St Dominic, the Black Friars.

clue.text: Spoke about Conservative extremist

indicators.note: going around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a radial is a spoke radiating from a hub

explanation.surface: Someone talked about a Tory who holds extreme views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' reads as the past of speak, but is a wheel's spoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical holds extreme views and wants sweeping change, a person at the political fringe.

clue.text: Assembling for a light meal

definitions.meaning: gathering pages or information together in order
a snack or simple repast, often cold

explanation.definitionFit: It means the act of gathering and ordering material, and also a light, often cold, meal.

clue.text: Noble resistance in the Resistance

indicators.note: placed in, so one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: the Maquis was the French Resistance in the Second World War
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An aristocrat put up a fight within the wartime resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquis is a nobleman ranking above an earl, a member of the aristocracy.

clue.text: Stunning Melissa making the earth move?

indicators.note: stunned letters are knocked about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gorgeous woman called Melissa makes the earth move for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making the earth move' is the idiom for a thrilling romance, but here it is literal: an earthquake.
explanation.definitionFit: Seismal is an adjective meaning relating to earthquakes, ground tremors that shake the land.

clue.text: Mike has trouble getting good deal for sports top

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to ail is to be unwell or troubled
a lot is a large amount

explanation.surface: Mike struggles to get a bargain on a sports shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good deal' looks like a bargain, but means a great quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: A maillot is a jersey worn by cyclists, as in the yellow jersey of the Tour de France.

clue.text: Tanner needs this nail hammered into pieces

indicators.note: placed into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: chess pieces are called men

indicators.note: beaten about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A leather tanner needs a nail hammered into bits.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner here is not a leather worker but someone getting a suntan; chess pieces are called men.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin pigment that darkens on exposure to sun, so it is what someone going brown relies on.

clue.text: Shock problem isn't resolved

indicators.note: dissolved and reformed, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sudden difficulty has not been sorted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' is a thick mass of hair, not a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Lice eggs infest hair, so a shock of hair can suffer from these parasites.

clue.text: Scot's title of one article covering another

indicators.note: lying over, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: the definite article in English
the indefinite article, another article of grammar

explanation.surface: A Scottish title appears on one piece of writing covering another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' suggests a newspaper piece; it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: A thane was a Scottish clan chief or lord, as in Macbeth, Thane of Cawdor.

clue.text: Community keeps a German in subservient state

indicators.note: holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a village is a small rural community
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: A town holds a German in servitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A villein was a feudal serf, and villeinage was that bound, servile condition.

clue.text: Furnish menus, dinner regularly brought round

indicators.note: turned round, so the letters read in the opposite direction
at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Menus at dinner are routinely handed round the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters E, U, D, N, E; 'brought round' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to provide or endow someone with a quality, to equip them.

clue.text: With a will, this is proverbially found out

definitions.text: With a will, this is proverbially found
definitions.meaning: from the proverb 'where there's a will there's a ...', meaning determination finds means

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says where there's a will there's this; on its own it means absent or not here.

clue.text: Daily newspaper's rejected by top executive

indicators.note: thrown out by, so the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a chairwoman heads a company board
the i is a British national newspaper

explanation.surface: A daily paper is turned down by the head of the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper but is British for a daily cleaner. The 's after 'newspaper' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a daily is a cleaning woman who comes in every day to do housework.

clue.text: Harmonic structure I incorporated into jazz style

indicators.note: taken into the body of something, so placed inside

parts.note: trad is traditional jazz

explanation.surface: A musician has worked a chord into some traditional jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a chord of three notes, a root, third and fifth, forms the basic harmony.

clue.text: Unfortunate female born with case of dropsy

parts.note: née is used of a woman's maiden name, meaning born

indicators.note: the outer case of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A poor woman was born with a case of the dropsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' looks like an illness, but takes the outside letters D and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The unfortunate in society are the poor, those lacking money and in want.

clue.text: Left running country house over quite some time

parts.note: a machine that is running is on
a grange is a country house with farm buildings

explanation.surface: Someone left the country house running for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-range plans or forecasts extend far into the future, covering a lengthy period.
